text:
Helen Zille Rows Boat in Flooded Soweto to Protest Drainage Failures
Helen Zille, the Democratic Alliance’s mayoral candidate for Johannesburg, kayaked through a flooded street in Soweto this week to highlight long-standing failures in the area’s drainage infrastructure.
During the demonstration, Zille claimed that the City of Johannesburg spent only 26% of its capital budget during the 2025/26 financial year. She asserted that funds designated for critical projects, including stormwater infrastructure, were either mismanaged or stolen, urging residents to register to vote for a DA-led government.
Infrastructure demonstrations
The Soweto event is part of a series of public demonstrations by Zille targeting municipal service failures in Johannesburg. In a previous instance, Zille wore a swimming cap and aqualung cup to swim in a large pothole in Douglasdale. The pothole had developed over three years as a result of a burst pipe that the city had left unrepaired. Following that specific event, the City of Johannesburg responded by repairing the steel pipe.
Zille also visited Limbro Park to document a burst pipe that had been gushing millions of liters of water for nearly a week. During that visit, she highlighted the waste of water occurring amidst broader water infrastructure issues within the city.
Public and municipal response
The campaign tactics have met with mixed reactions. While some reports indicate that the demonstrations have prompted immediate municipal action in certain areas, other residents have expressed disapproval. Some Soweto residents described the river rafting demonstration as the work of a “sgebengu.”
Zille continues to promote her candidacy for mayor of Johannesburg under the campaign hashtag #BelieveInJoburg, focusing on the demand to fix city infrastructure.
The City of Johannesburg has not issued a formal response to the specific budget spending allegations raised during the Soweto demonstration.
